bugs.name: Moving a Tasks Kanban card hides its relation chip until refetch
bugs.summary: Moving a task between Kanban status columns removes its visible related-person chip until the record is refetched, while the relation remains saved.
bugs.expected: Moving a task to another status column preserves the related-person chip displayed on its card.
bugs.actual: The status change persists, but the related-person chip disappears after mouse or keyboard movement and stays absent while waiting. Reloading the board or opening the task record restores the chip without changing its saved relation.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace, open Tasks, and create a uniquely named task linked to a person.
Create a uniquely named Kanban view grouped by Status. Enable Relations under Options > Fields so the related-person chip appears on the task card.
Reload the board once after creating the task and confirm the chip is visible.
Drag the task from To do to In progress. Wait for the update and observe that the status changes but the relation chip disappears.
Reload the board or open the task record. Confirm the chip returns and the changed status remains saved.
Move the same card back with keyboard navigation: Space to pick up, ArrowLeft toward To do, and Space to drop. Observe the relation chip disappear again.

bugs.name: Saved views can be created with an empty name
bugs.summary: Creating a saved view with an empty or whitespace-only name produces a persistent unlabeled entry in the view selector.
bugs.expected: Creating a saved view requires a nonempty name or assigns a usable default name.
bugs.actual: Creation succeeds with an empty name. After reload the selector shows an icon-only entry, the header shows only its icon and record count, and the browser title falls back to the object name. Multiple unnamed views are visually indistinguishable, although their records remain accessible and renaming works.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies.
Open the current view selector, choose Add view, and leave Table selected.
Clear the view-name input and select Create new view.
Reload the page and open the view selector. Observe that the new view remains unnamed, with an icon-only entry and no view name in the header.
Repeat with another empty name or a whitespace-only name to observe multiple indistinguishable unnamed entries.

bugs.name: Calendar views ignore selected record sorting
bugs.summary: Calendar cards stay in their existing position order when the selected record sort changes, even after saving and reloading the view.
bugs.expected: Calendar records follow the selected ascending or descending sort, including after the setting is saved and the view is reloaded.
bugs.actual: The sort chip changes direction and the setting saves successfully, but Calendar cards keep the same position order under ascending and descending sorts. Reloading preserves the selected direction without applying it. Table views correctly reorder the same records.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies. Create a uniquely named Calendar view using Creation date.
Navigate to a date containing multiple companies with distinct names, or create a few uniquely named companies on the same date to provide an isolated comparison.
Apply a Name ascending sort and note the card order. Change the active sort to descending and observe that the cards remain in the same order despite the changed direction indicator.
Select Update view and reload. Confirm that the descending sort indicator persists while the Calendar still ignores the selected ordering.
Use a separate Table view to compare the same records under Name ascending and descending; the Table reorders correctly.
Repeat in a People Calendar using Creation date and Name > First name to observe the same ignored sort direction.

bugs.name: Switching to Kanban silently discards pending list filters
bugs.summary: Changing the layout of the current saved view silently replaces its applied but unsaved filters and sorts with saved settings.
bugs.expected: Changing the layout of the same view retains its active filters and pending changes, or warns before discarding them.
bugs.actual: A Table filtered to matching companies loses its filter chip and Reset/Update view controls when switched to Kanban, without leaving the current view or warning. Switching back to Table shows the unfiltered list. A People case also loses pending filtering and sorting. A Calendar-to-Table control retains its pending filter.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies. Create a uniquely named Table view.
Apply a Name Contains filter for an existing company, such as Microsoft. Confirm that matching rows, the filter chip, and Reset/Update view controls appear. Do not save the view.
Choose Options > Layout > Kanban. Observe that the active filter chip and pending-change controls disappear without a warning while the same saved view remains selected.
Switch back to Table and confirm that the filter remains absent and other companies are visible.
Repeat on a separate People Table view with a Name Contains filter, such as Mark, and a pending sort to observe the same loss of active changes.

bugs.name: Grouped table disables its Group by control
bugs.summary: Grouping a Table view with only one eligible grouping field disables Group by, making the None option inaccessible.
bugs.expected: A Table view can remove its grouping through Group by > None, even when only one eligible grouping field exists.
bugs.actual: After grouping Companies by Account Owner or People by Company, the Group by row becomes disabled and does not respond to mouse or keyboard. None cannot be reached, including after reload or reselecting Table. Switching Table to Kanban and back clears grouping as a workaround.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies. Create a uniquely named Table view.
Open Options > Group and confirm that the field picker offers None and Account Owner.
Select Account Owner, then close and reopen Options > Group.
Try to open Group by Account Owner. Observe that it is disabled and None is inaccessible.
Reload the view or reselect the Table layout and confirm that the grouping control remains disabled.
Repeat on a separate People Table view grouped by Company to observe the same failure.

bugs.name: Shift-selecting a row range excludes the clicked endpoint from selection
bugs.summary: Shift-clicking a table row range leaves the clicked endpoint visibly checked but excludes it from the selected count and bulk-action targets.
bugs.expected: Shift-clicking from the first row to the fifth selects all five rows, with checkboxes, row highlighting, selected count, and bulk-action targets agreeing.
bugs.actual: All five checkboxes appear checked, but the header reports 4 selected and the clicked endpoint lacks selected shading. Bulk updating changes only four records, leaving the checked endpoint unchanged after reload. The same mismatch occurs upward and in a two-row People result.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies in a Table view. Reload to clear selection.
Click the checkbox for the first visible row, then hold Shift and click the checkbox itself for the fifth visible row.
Observe five checked boxes, but 4 selected in the header and no selected shading on the clicked fifth row.
Clear selection and repeat upward from the fifth row to the first; the clicked first row is similarly excluded.
As a control, select the five rows with individual checkbox clicks and confirm that the count becomes 5 selected.

For an isolated functional check, repeat the Shift-click range on five disposable test companies and bulk-update their City field. Confirm that the action targets four records and that the endpoint retains its previous value after reload.

bugs.name: Domain Name Doesn’t contain excludes companies with an unset link label
bugs.summary: A negative Domain Name filter incorrectly excludes companies whose populated domain matches the criterion but whose optional link label is unset.
bugs.expected: Domain Name Doesn’t contain .com includes a populated .org or other non-.com URL even when the URL has no optional link label.
bugs.actual: Contains .com correctly selects the .com company, but switching to Doesn’t contain excludes the unlabeled .org company and can leave an isolated pair with no results. Seeded Google with domain goo.gle is also wrongly excluded. A nonmatching URL with a populated link label can remain visible, so exclusion is conditional rather than universal.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies. Create two uniquely named disposable companies, one with a .org Domain Name URL and one with a .com URL. Leave their optional link labels unset.
Filter Name to the unique prefix so both test companies are visible.
Add Domain Name Contains .com and confirm that only the .com company remains.
Change that filter to Doesn’t contain .com. Observe that no test companies appear, although the .org company should match.
Reset the Domain Name filter and confirm that both companies return. Repeat the positive/negative sequence to confirm the result.
As a seeded-data comparison, verify that Google with domain goo.gle is visible unfiltered but omitted under Domain Name Doesn’t contain .com.

bugs.name: Moving an opportunity between Kanban columns breaks its active sort
bugs.summary: Changing an opportunity’s Kanban stage replaces the destination column’s active sort with manual-position ordering until the board is refetched.
bugs.expected: After moving an opportunity between columns, the destination column continues to follow the selected sort.
bugs.actual: A board sorted by Close date or Name becomes incorrectly ordered after a stage change, while the selected sort indicator remains active. Keyboard column moves and side-panel Stage edits reproduce the problem. Reloading restores the correct order; no saved-sort corruption or record loss was observed.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named Opportunities Kanban view grouped by Stage.
Create three uniquely named disposable opportunities with distinct Close dates in one stage. Apply and save Close date ascending, then reload to confirm the correct sorted order.
Move one opportunity into another column using keyboard pickup and column navigation, then move it back to the original populated column.
Observe that the destination column is no longer ordered by Close date even though its ascending sort indicator remains active.
Reload the board and confirm that the correct order returns.
Repeat by changing an opportunity’s Stage through its side panel to observe the same destination-column sort loss.

bugs.name: Record-page navigation ignores Search any field filtering
bugs.summary: Record-page Next/Previous omits the originating list’s Search any field query and navigates to records outside the matching results.
bugs.expected: Opening a record from a searched list preserves that search context for the record counter and Next/Previous navigation.
bugs.actual: A searched list contains only matching records, but opening a match shows a counter for the larger list and Next/Previous reaches unrelated records. The same result set filtered through a normal Name Contains filter paginates correctly. The searched list itself remains filtered when returning.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named Opportunities view and two disposable opportunities sharing a unique searchable name prefix.
Apply Search any field using that prefix and confirm that only the two matching records are shown. Save and reload the view to confirm that the search persists.
Open one matching opportunity as a full record page. Observe that its navigation counter represents a larger set than the two matching results.
Use Next/Previous and confirm that navigation can reach an opportunity whose name and content do not match the search.
Return to the originating list and confirm that its search results remain filtered.
As a control, replace Search any field with a normal Name Contains filter for the same prefix. Open a matching record and verify that the counter and Next/Previous stay within the two matches.

bugs.name: Search any field omits saved Task and Note Body text
bugs.summary: Search any field does not find saved text in a Task or Note Body, while matching title text is searchable.
bugs.expected: Search any field finds a Task or Note whose saved Body contains the query, even when its title does not.
bugs.actual: A unique query present only in the saved Body returns no matching record. Searching for a unique title word finds the same record. The Body-only omission persists after reload and reproduces in Tasks and Notes.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named disposable Task.
Give the Task a title containing one unique marker and save a different unique marker only in its Body. Reload or reopen the Task to confirm that the Body text persisted.
Return to the Tasks list and apply Search any field using the Body-only marker. Observe that the Task is missing.
Replace the query with the title marker and confirm that the same Task appears.
Repeat with another saved Task and with a Note whose unique query appears only in its Body.

bugs.name: Point of Contact filter cannot find Kimberly Gordon, who is displayed on a matching opportunity
bugs.summary: Point of Contact filter search fails for an existing contact’s full displayed name, while either individual name part finds the same contact.
bugs.expected: The Point of Contact filter picker finds a contact using the full name displayed on the opportunity, allowing that contact to be selected.
bugs.actual: Searching the full name Kimberly Gordon returns No results even though the contact exists and is displayed on an opportunity. Searching Kimberly or Gordon finds her, and the relation edit picker also accepts the full name. The same failure reproduces with fresh contacts.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace, open Opportunities, and create a uniquely named disposable Table view.
Locate an opportunity displaying a contact with both first and last names, such as Kimberly Gordon.
Add a Point of Contact filter and enter the contact’s full displayed name in its picker search.
Observe No results, then search just the first name or last name and confirm that the same contact appears and can be selected.
Open the contact relation editor on the opportunity and verify that searching the full name finds the contact there.

bugs.name: Saved multi-sort priority changes from Company-first to Amount-first after refresh
bugs.summary: Saving multiple new sorts together can change their priority after reload, changing the view’s record order even though sort directions are retained.
bugs.expected: A saved view retains the configured sort priority after reload: Company ascending remains primary and Amount descending remains secondary.
bugs.actual: After saving and reloading, Company ascending then Amount descending can become Amount descending then Company ascending. The changed priority changes the actual record order. The defect is intermittent and also occurs with other objects, three sorts, and creating a view from current settings.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace, open Opportunities, and create a uniquely named disposable Table view.
Add Company ascending first, then Amount descending, before saving either new sort. Confirm Company is the primary sort and Amount orders records within each company.
Click Update view to save both sorts together, then reload. If the first reload retains locally cached sort metadata, reload again.

Observe whether the sort chips reverse to Amount descending then Company ascending and the records become primarily ordered by Amount. Repeat with a fresh view if the intermittent ordering change does not occur.
As a control, save the first sort before adding and separately saving the second sort; confirm that this preserves the configured priority.

bugs.name: Amount-filtered Kanban move errors and fails to save with partially cached opportunities
bugs.summary: Moving an opportunity in an Amount-filtered Kanban can throw an amountMicros error before saving when the record was previously loaded without its Amount field. The card appears to move, but totals stay stale and reload restores its old stage.
bugs.expected: A supported Kanban stage move saves the new stage and refreshes column totals without an error, including after navigating from a view that hides Amount.
bugs.actual: The card appears in the destination column, but a toast says Cannot read properties of undefined (reading amountMicros). No stage update is saved, column sums remain unchanged and reloading returns the card to its original stage. Fully cached cards and moves without the Amount filter can save correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a fresh opportunity with a populated Amount and stage New.
Create a disposable Opportunities Table view with Amount hidden and no Amount filter. Load the opportunity there.

Navigate in the app to a disposable Kanban grouped by Stage with an Amount filter that includes that opportunity, such as Amount greater than or equal to 2,800,000. Configure Sum Amount column summaries.
Move the previously loaded opportunity from New to Meeting. If the opportunity is already fully cached with Amount, repeat using a fresh opportunity and the Table-to-Kanban setup.
Observe the amountMicros error, the card appearing in Meeting and unchanged column sums.
Reload and observe that the opportunity returns to New, confirming the move was not saved. As a control, remove the Amount filter and verify that moving the same card saves.

bugs.name: Readding a saved sort makes Update view fail with Migration execution failed
bugs.summary: Removing a saved sort and adding the same field back makes Update view fail. The replacement sort does not save, while other changes can partially persist.
bugs.expected: Update view saves a valid replacement sort, including a changed direction, without an error.
bugs.actual: Update view displays Migration execution failed after a saved sort is removed and the same field is added again. The replacement fails to save and the old sort can remain after reload. Other sorts added in the same update can persist despite the error. Multiple sorts are not required to trigger the failure.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named Companies Table view.
Add a Name ascending sort and save it with Update view.
Remove the saved Name sort, then add Name again before saving. Choose descending to make the replacement distinguishable. Optionally add an Account Owner sort as well.
Click Update view and observe the Migration execution failed error.
Reload and observe that the replacement Name sort was not saved; another added sort can have persisted.
As a control, change the direction on the existing saved sort without removing and readding it, then confirm that Update view succeeds.

bugs.name: Browser Back from a record resets the long table to the top
bugs.summary: Returning with browser Back from a full record page loses the browsing position in a long ungrouped table, while the record-page breadcrumb returns near the opened row.
bugs.expected: Browser Back returns near the opened record when that position is within the initially loaded table range, so browsing can continue. Exact pixel restoration is unnecessary.
bugs.actual: Browser Back resets the table to its first row, including when the record was opened about 1,500 pixels down. Returning through the record-page breadcrumb instead restores the opened row near its previous position. This occurs on tablet and desktop, in Companies and People.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open a long, ungrouped Companies Table view.
Scroll about 1,500 pixels down and note a visible company.
Open that company in its full record page. If a side panel opens first, use its Open action.
Use browser Back and observe that the table starts at its first row rather than near the company you opened.
Repeat from the same position, returning with the record-page breadcrumb instead. Observe that the opened company is brought back into view.

bugs.name: Switching a grouped view to Calendar hides all events until reload
bugs.summary: Changing a grouped Table or Kanban view to Calendar produces a blank calendar even though Creation date is selected and records exist in the displayed month.
bugs.expected: Switching to Calendar displays records on the selected Creation date, including records previously visible in the grouped view, without requiring a reload or date-field reselection.
bugs.actual: Calendar displays no events or overflow links after the layout switch, while the menu still shows Creation date. Reloading the same view or selecting Creation date again restores events. Ungrouped Table-to-Calendar switching works. The failure reproduces for People grouped by Company and Companies grouped by Account Owner.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named People Table view containing records created in the month you will inspect.
Group the view by Company. Records without a company remain visible under No Value; adding relation groups is unnecessary.
Switch through Kanban, then choose Options > Layout > Calendar. A direct grouped Table-to-Calendar switch can also reproduce the failure.

Confirm Date field is Creation date, End date field is None, and the displayed month includes the records' creation dates. Observe that Calendar contains no events, including for people visible in No Value before the switch.
Reload the same view without changing its settings and observe that events appear. Selecting Creation date again also restores them.
As a control, switch a fresh ungrouped Table view directly to Calendar and confirm that its dated records appear.

bugs.name: Closing Options immediately after renaming a view silently loses the rename
bugs.summary: Closing the Options menu within about 500 milliseconds of editing a saved view name discards the pending rename. Pressing Enter before closing does not commit it.
bugs.expected: A changed view name is saved when Enter is pressed or the Options editor closes, without requiring an undocumented pause.
bugs.actual: The editor contains the replacement name, including after Enter, but immediate closure leaves the old saved name in the view selector and reopened Options. Reload retains the old name. Waiting for the debounce before closing saves correctly; the view-selector Edit flow also works.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named People Table view.
Open Options and replace its name with a different distinctive name.
Immediately close the menu by clicking outside, within about 500 milliseconds of the final edit. Pressing Enter immediately before closing also reproduces the loss.
Reopen Options and observe that the selector and editor still show the previous name. Reload and confirm the replacement was not saved.
As a control, enter a replacement name, wait at least one second before closing Options, and confirm that it remains saved.

bugs.name: Creating a view from current settings replaces Last name sorting with First name
bugs.summary: Creating a new People view from current settings drops the selected Name sort subfield, replacing Last name sorting with First name and changing the persisted row order.
bugs.expected: A view created from current settings preserves the selected Name subfield, sort direction and filters.
bugs.actual: The source view has Name · Last name descending, but the copied view has Name · First name descending and a different row order. The filter and descending direction remain intact, and the changed sorting persists after reload. Normal Update view preserves the Last name choice.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named People Table view.
Choose a Name sort using Last name descending and save it with Update view. Note the order of people with distinguishable first and last names.
Add a Name Is not empty filter, leaving a pending view change.
Use the arrow beside Update view, choose Create view, give the new view a unique name and complete creation.
Observe that the filter remains but the sort chip now says Name · First name and the ordinary records are ordered by first name instead of last name. Descending direction remains selected.
Reload the copied view and confirm that the First name sort persists. Return to the source view and confirm that its Last name sort remains intact.

bugs.name: Calendar views silently hide most tasks sharing a due date
bugs.summary: Calendar Month and Day views silently cap displayed tasks at five and ten respectively, without an overflow control, even when 150 matching tasks share that date. Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): A Due Date calendar omits tasks beyond a small display cap, without a way to load them. The seeded October 10 date has 150 matching tasks; Month displays five, and Week/Day display ten. Filtering for an omitted task makes it appear. Count this as the same reference rather than a separate bug.
bugs.expected: All matching tasks should be accessible on their due date, either in the calendar itself or through a visible overflow control.
bugs.actual: The filtered table contains 150 distinct 'Prepare meeting agenda' tasks, all due Oct 10, 2026 at 9:20 PM. Month displays only five and Day only ten. Scrolling the complete calendar containers reveals no further events or overflow controls.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Tasks > All Tasks.
Filter Title to Contains 'Prepare meeting agenda'.
Observe 150 matching tasks; scroll the table to verify their due dates are Oct 10, 2026 at 9:20 PM.
Create a Calendar view using Due Date as its date field and apply the same title filter.
Open October 2026 in Month view; observe only five tasks on Oct 10 with no overflow control.
Switch to Day view and navigate to Oct 10; observe only ten tasks.
Scroll the full calendar container; the remaining matching tasks are still inaccessible.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Sign in and open Tasks > All Tasks.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Filter Title Contains Prepare meeting agenda; observe 150 matching tasks with Due Date Oct 10, 2026 6:04 PM.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Create a Tasks view via view dropdown > Add view, select Calendar, and select Due Date as its date field.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Display October 2026 in Month mode; observe only five cards on October10.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Switch to Week covering October4–10, then Day and navigate to October10; observe only ten cards.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Scroll the Day view to the bottom; observe no additional cards or load-more control.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Apply an Id filter for 20202020-0054-4e7c-8001-123456789def; observe this previously omitted task appears on October10.
Reported variant (codex-30m-twenty-12): Reset the filter; observe it disappears again among the capped ten cards.

bugs.name: By Status task board silently hides tasks with No Status
bugs.summary: The built-in By Status board excludes tasks assigned the selectable No Status value, with no uncategorized group available. They remain in All Tasks and in a newly created Kanban view's No Value group.
bugs.expected: Tasks with No Status should remain accessible in an uncategorized column, or have a visible way to enable that group.
bugs.actual: The task remains in All Tasks but disappears from By Status. The board offers only To do, In progress and Done groups; its Group options have no No Value or hidden-group option. A new Kanban view does display the same task in No Value.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Tasks > All Tasks.
Create a uniquely named test task and open its full record.
Open Status and choose No Status.
Return to All Tasks and confirm the task appears with blank Status.
Switch the view dropdown to By Status.
Observe the task is absent from all columns.
Open Options > Group and observe there is no No Value or hidden-group option to reveal it.
As a control, create a new Kanban Tasks view; its No Value column contains the task.

bugs.name: Selecting a second own company row replaces the first selection instead of adding to it
bugs.summary: The Companies table cannot retain two selected owned rows: selecting the second replaces the first. The precise reported post-click state differed—the second row was checked and the count stayed at one—but multi-selection still failed.
bugs.expected: After selecting MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-A and then MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-B, both checkboxes should remain checked and the selected count should become two.
bugs.actual: The first row was checked and the count showed 1 selected. After clicking the second row's checkbox, the second row was checked, the first was unchecked, and the count remained 1. This state persisted after six seconds. The reported detail that the second checkbox also remained unchecked and the count disappeared did not occur in the verified pass.
reproSteps: Load the supplied authenticated state for the Tim Apple account (no credentials entered) and open /objects/companies.

Using the visible New Company action, create two fresh company records and name them MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-A and MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-B. Confirm each detail panel shows Created by Tim Apple; use only these fixtures.
Click the checkbox for MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-A. Observe its checked state and the “1 selected” indicator.
Click the checkbox for MULTISELECT-MO-7Q9D-B. Observe that B becomes checked, A becomes unchecked, and the count remains 1.
Leave the table on that state for six seconds and observe that it persists.

bugs.name: List Members page stays blank despite containing records
bugs.summary: The List Members journey reports a nonzero count but renders no table, column headers or record rows. Options opens an empty menu and Create View cannot configure a usable view.
bugs.expected: Memberships appear in a browsable table with list/person relations; view options provide usable configuration.
bugs.actual: All · 1 reports the membership, but the area below the toolbar has no columns or rows even after reload. Options expands an empty listbox; Create View cannot proceed and reports 'Current view ID and record index ID are required to create new view'. The imported membership is confirmed on the List's Members and Person's Lists relations. Parent independently reproduced the blank page.
reproSteps: Create a test List and Person, or use prepared List 041125e8-a8ee-4a05-b553-fec07cb7c5e9 and QA Ada Explorer c5024755-4f1a-46ca-9f9d-60a279c6e65d.
Open Command Menu → Go to List Members → Ctrl+K → Import List Members.
Import CSV with headers List (ID),Person (ID) and a row containing those test UUIDs; map List > Id and Person > Id and complete import.
Return to /objects/messageListMembers, wait for loading, and reload.
Click Options; also try Command Menu → Create View.

bugs.name: Task and Note relation searches fail because they filter a nonexistent name field
bugs.summary: Searching a Task or Note in relation-filter pickers returns an invalid-filter error and no results, preventing selection of existing matching records.
bugs.expected: The picker searches the related records' titles and offers matching notes/tasks for filtering.
bugs.actual: Note search displays No results and toast 'Invalid filter : note object doesn't have any "name" field.' Task search similarly reports the task object has no name field. Empty search lists recent records, but searching their titles fails.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a note with a distinctive title, or use existing Meeting Follow-up.
Open Command Menu and choose Go to Note Targets.
Click Filter, choose Note, then enter the known note title in the picker search box.
Wait for the results. Repeat with Go to Task Targets → Filter → Task and an existing task title.

bugs.name: Table row selections clear after an unrelated saved-view rename
bugs.summary: Selected table rows become unchecked when a different saved view is renamed in another tab, despite leaving the selected table untouched.
bugs.expected: An unrelated saved-view rename should preserve selected rows and the selection count in the current table.
bugs.actual: The selected Companies row becomes unchecked and the selected count disappears after the unrelated view rename. Quiet controls retained their selection.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Companies > All Companies in a table view.
Select a company using its row checkbox and confirm the row is checked and the selected count is one.
Open a second tab in the same browser session and navigate to Notes.
Use the view picker to rename a Notes saved view and save the change.
Return to the Companies tab without changing its filters, view, or selection. Observe the checked row becomes unchecked and the selection count disappears.

bugs.name: Advanced filter value search leaks into the field picker and hides its choices
bugs.summary: After searching for an Account Owner value, the same search text remains in the advanced-filter field picker and hides unrelated field choices.
bugs.expected: Opening the field picker should show available fields without retaining text entered in the separate value picker.
bugs.actual: After searching Tim and selecting Tim Apple, the field picker opens with Tim as its search text and no field choices. Clearing that text restores the choices. The picker does open; the original claim that it remains collapsed was not reproduced.
reproSteps: Sign in and open People in a fresh custom table view.
Open Filter > Advanced filter and choose Company > Account Owner as the rule field.
Open the value picker, search Tim, and select Tim Apple.
Click outside the advanced filter, then reopen its rule chip.
Open the Company > Account Owner field selector to change the field. Observe that Tim remains in the field search and no field choices appear.
Clear Tim from the field search and observe that the field choices return.

bugs.name: Changing a saved advanced-filter field persists new values under the old field
bugs.summary: Changing an existing saved filter from Amount to Stage saves the Stage values but retains the old Amount field. Reloading displays raw Stage values under Amount and returns no matching records.
bugs.expected: Update view should persist the changed field together with its operator and values, so reload restores the same Stage filter and matching rows shown in the preview.
bugs.actual: The Stage preview returns matching rows, but after a completed Update view and reload the rule reads Amount Is not ["PROPOSAL","CUSTOMER"] and returns zero rows. The field-save failure and raw-value display are symptoms of the same omitted field change.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Opportunities Table view.
Add an advanced Amount Is not 450000 rule, save the view, and wait for saving to complete.
Edit that existing rule by changing its field to Stage, choosing Is not, and selecting Proposal and Customer.
Confirm the preview contains matching opportunities.
Close the filter editor, click Update view, and wait for saving to finish.
Reload and reopen the advanced rule. Observe Amount Is not ["PROPOSAL","CUSTOMER"] rather than Stage Is not Proposal, Customer, with zero matching rows.
As a control, remove the corrupted rule and create a new Stage Is not Proposal, Customer rule; save and reload to observe that this newly created rule persists correctly.

bugs.name: Grouped table calculations include records excluded by the active filter
bugs.summary: Filtering a Stage-grouped Opportunities table to one stage removes the other stages’ rows, but their empty groups still show Amount averages and other calculations from excluded records.
bugs.expected: Each group calculation should respect both the active view filter and the group condition. Groups with no matching records should not display values calculated from excluded records.
bugs.actual: With Stage Is Meeting applied, only Meeting rows remain, while empty New and Screening groups still show Amount averages such as 547k and 546.3k. The incorrect calculations persist after saving and reloading; Sum and Earliest Close date also include excluded records.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Opportunities Table view.
Group the table by Stage and leave empty groups visible.
Set the Amount group-footer calculation to Average.
Apply the single filter Stage Is Meeting.
Observe that only Meeting contains rows, but empty New, Screening and other excluded groups still display nonzero Amount averages.
Save the view, wait for saving to complete, and reload. Observe that the incorrect group calculations persist.

Apply a single basic Name Contains filter for the unique prefix. Set the Emails footer to Unique and verify the rows, count and calculation agree for the three people.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report plus independent Claude Code and Codex browser reproductions and source audits, coordinator citation checks, and user acceptance.

reproSteps: Create a fresh Opportunities Table view, apply a Name sort, and click Update view.
Immediately after the save receives a successful server response, hard-reload the page. The trigger is intermittent and requires a near-instant reload before client synchronization completes.
In an affected trial, observe the missing sort chip, default row ordering and Update view offered without a new edit. Confirm the refreshed server view metadata still contains the acknowledged sort.
Click that offered Update view. Observe a successful DestroyViewSort for the retained sort and confirm that later reloads remain unsorted with no saved sort.
As a control, repeat with a fresh view but wait several seconds after saving before reload; the sort and correct ordering remain, with no spurious Update view.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report plus independent Claude Code and Codex browser reproductions and source audits, coordinator citation checks, and user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Observed broken functionality or unintended loss of saved configuration.

The coordinator checked the cache, initialization, difference calculation, deletion request and backend deletion paths. Exact interrupted-cache timing remains inferred. Latest retains these source paths; latest runtime was not tested.
Existing unfinished-save negative references explicitly exclude a later Update click removing retained configuration. The user approved this tightly timed destructive scope.

bugs.name: Text Contains filters interpret literal percent and underscore as SQL wildcards
bugs.summary: Ordinary UI Contains and Does not contain filters interpret typed percent and underscore as SQL wildcard syntax, including records without the typed punctuation or excluding them incorrectly.
bugs.expected: The UI text operators should match the entered text literally, case-insensitively, rather than expose undocumented SQL wildcard syntax. This expectation concerns conversion of UI values; raw API pattern operators retain their intended wildcard semantics.
bugs.actual: Name Contains QA% matches QA Alpha and QA Beta although neither name contains a percent sign. Job Title Does not contain 50% excludes a person whose title is 50 off, without a percent sign. Underscore also acts as a one-character wildcard. Ordinary-text controls return the expected records.
reproSteps: Create fresh People with a unique common name prefix, for example QA Alpha and QA Beta, with neither name containing a percent sign.
Apply Name > Contains > QA%. Observe names lacking the literal percent sign still included. Compare an ordinary matching prefix and a nonexistent prefix.
Give a fresh person Job Title 50 off, without a percent sign. Apply Job Title > Does not contain > 50%. Observe the person incorrectly excluded despite not containing that literal text.
Compare a record actually containing a percent sign and ordinary-text filters. Repeat on fresh data; saving and reloading the filtered view retains the pattern behavior.
For underscore, compare names differing by one character and apply a Contains value with an underscore in that position; observe the underscore acts as a wildcard rather than requiring the character.
bugs.sourceCause: The shared UI filter converter interpolates raw text into percent-wrapped ILIKE patterns, including composite-name tokens, without escaping user-entered percent or underscore. The server correctly evaluates those supplied patterns.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo report plus independent Claude Code and Codex browser reproductions and source audits, coordinator citation checks, and user acceptance.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Observed broken functionality; controls using the same saved data work.
analysis: Claude and Codex independently recommended acceptance at severity 3 and reproduced positive Name filtering on fresh records with passing ordinary-text controls. Claude also verified wrong exclusion through the Job Title negative filter and a literal-percent control; Codex verified saved views, another user and desktop/tablet behavior.

The inspected SQL path binds filter values as parameters. No SQL injection, executable SQL manipulation, authorization bypass or saved-data loss was demonstrated. The accepted issue is UI matching correctness.

Merged API PR 17825 deliberately leaves wildcard control with API callers. That does not establish that an ordinary UI Contains field intentionally exposes pattern syntax. Later internal matcher wildcard-parity fixes concern the lower-level pattern contract.

Official UI docs now describe Contains as case-insensitive partial-text matching without documenting wildcard input. PR 28479 added that wording on 2026-10-20, after the fixture pin; it supports current semantics without conclusively establishing historical punctuation intent.

PR 23228, opened before the fixture pin, identifies this same plain-text list-filter problem and proposes escaping existing Contains and Does-not-contain values. It closed unmerged for unanswered review comments and no linked issue. It is contributor evidence, not maintainer approval or an explicit rejection of literal semantics.

The coordinator docs/PR investigation favors an unintended UI defect with moderate confidence. The user accepted the case after reviewing those limits. Latest source retains unescaped UI interpolation; latest runtime was not tested.
limitations: No explicit maintainer ruling on literal versus wildcard punctuation in UI Contains was located; the accepted literal-text contract remains an inference supported by docs and the matching proposal.
The clearer current documentation postdates the 2026-07-30 fixture source; the matching pre-pin PR was not merged.
Do not use this entry to classify intentional raw API wildcard matching as a bug or to claim SQL injection.
Name positive filtering and the plain-text Job Title negative filter were reproduced; broader shared converter callers are inferred rather than required matching scope.
No crash or saved-data loss was observed. Latest was inspected in source only.

bugs.name: Changing a saved Name filter to a relative date rule fails because its old field is retained
bugs.summary: Changing the field of an already-saved advanced rule omits its new field ID from the update, causing valid incompatible-type rules to fail validation against the old field.
bugs.expected: Saving a changed advanced-filter field should persist that field together with its valid operator and value.

Edit that saved rule by changing its field to Creation date and choosing Is relative → This day.
Save the updated view and observe the unsupported-operand error.
Reload and observe that the original Name filter remains saved.
Control: create a new Creation date Is relative This day rule directly; save and reload to confirm it persists.

matchingGuidance.distinction: N46 covers compatible-operator field changes that save new values silently under the old field. This entry covers incompatible field/operator changes that are blocked with an explicit validation error.

reviewEvidence.basis: Mo evidence, independent Codex and Claude browser/source verification, coordinator checks and user approval as a related entry.

Both verified that a newly created, never-saved date rule saves and survives reload. The defect requires editing the field of an already-saved rule.
Requests omit the changed field ID while changing operand/value; server validation rejects IS_RELATIVE against FULL_NAME or CONTAINS against DATE_TIME.

reproSteps: Create three fresh Tasks with distinct Alpha, Beta and Gamma titles; put Alpha and Gamma in To do and Beta in No Value.

bugs.summary: On a People view with an advanced Company → Name text condition, New Person and Add New fail with an error instead of creating a record and opening its drawer.

The failure repeats after saving the filter and reloading. Removing the advanced relation condition, or a fresh-page basic Company selection control, restores creation.
reproSteps: Create a fresh People table view and apply an advanced Company → Name → Contains condition with an existing Company-name text.
Optionally combine it with a Name Contains condition or a supported OR group. Save and reload.
Click New Person and the table Add New row. Observe an error, unchanged list and no creation drawer.
Repeat the attempted create after a fresh reload.
Control: remove the advanced relation condition, or reload a view with a basic Company is selection. New Person creates a record and opens its drawer with a valid Company reference.
bugs.sourceCause: Creation-default conversion treats a relation-traversal text value as the source relation foreign key. Separately, the optimistic list matcher treats a nested relation filter as a UUID filter. Depending on the cached-query/filter shape, creation aborts in that client matcher or reaches server UUID validation with the wrong Company ID.

matchingGuidance.distinction: Covers People creation blocked by an advanced Company-name traversal filter. Exact toast text is not required. bugs.name: Company record pagination skips empty revenue in a revenue-sorted view
bugs.summary: Company record pages undercount a descending Annual Revenue view and wrap forward navigation before visiting its empty-revenue company.
bugs.expected: Record-page positions and Next navigation should include every matching company in the originating filtered and sorted view.
bugs.actual: A three-company view lists Gamma ($200), Beta ($100) and Alpha (empty). Gamma shows 1/2, Beta shows 2/2, and Next cycles between them without reaching Alpha. Opening Alpha separately or using Previous from Gamma reaches it with a contradictory 1/1 total. Removing the revenue sort or populating Alpha with $50 restores three-record traversal.
reproSteps: Create three fresh Companies named with a unique common prefix: Alpha with empty Annual Revenue, Beta with $100 and Gamma with $200.
Create a Company view filtered to the prefix, sort Annual Revenue descending and confirm all three rows are present.
Open Gamma through its row and the side-panel Open action. Observe the breadcrumb total 2 although the view contains 3.
Use Next repeatedly: Gamma leads to Beta, then wraps to Gamma without visiting Alpha.
Open Alpha separately or use Previous from Gamma: Alpha is accessible but shows 1/1. Repeat with another fresh dataset.
Controls: remove the revenue sort while retaining the filter, then confirm all three are reachable; with the sort restored and every revenue populated, confirm correct three-record traversal.
bugs.sourceCause: Record-page pagination constructs neighbor filters with ordinary greater-than/less-than comparisons and equality prefixes, without a branch for empty currency values under NULLS LAST ordering. Those neighbor queries omit the empty amount, so their summed counts understate the total and forward navigation wraps early.
